**Test image observations:**
- Very young soybean seedlings, completely collapsed and dead near soil level
- Leaves entirely brown/tan, dried, shriveled and curled — remain attached to stems
- Stems appear dark/brown at base near soil line
- Surrounding plants in background appear green and healthy
- Classic "pre- or post-emergence damping off" presentation at seedling stage

**Analysis:**
- The pattern of complete seedling collapse with brown wilted leaves remaining attached strongly matches **Phytophthora** — description: "Young plants show rapid yellowing and wilting with soft rot and collapse of the root... leaves typically stay attached after plant death"
- The Phytophthora reference image is a near-perfect match: same collapsed wilted brown leaves attached to stems, same field context with healthy plants nearby
- Pythium_damping_off would show water-soaked soft rot and soil sticking to rotted seeds — not matching the dry, crispy collapsed appearance here
- Rhizoctonia is possible but the complete plant collapse pattern with attached dead leaves fits Phytophthora better
